observations.observation: On Oct. 2, Culpium reported that TSMC was exploring possible ways to work with Terafab on its Texas factories. This was the earliest traceable public report found here, not an announced agreement.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The report cited sources and provided no signed terms, assigned operating role, production volume, or commitment.

observations.observation: Culpium’s Oct. 3 follow-up reported Musk describing the TSMC contact as discussions only, while leaving open that something might come of them. This qualified the earlier exploration report without confirming a deal.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The exact X-post time and timezone were not verified; the reported wording does not identify agreed terms or a selected partner.

observations.observation: Newsquawk’s feed carried Musk’s Oct. 7 statement that his companies would build and run the fab and that TSMC might sublease part. The page records the feed item at 06:38 UTC and publication at 06:58 UTC.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is a news relay, not the original X post. A possible sublease is not evidence that one was agreed, and the statement gives no Intel production scope.

observations.observation: A Benzinga article snapshot published at 09:02:08Z reported Tan saying Intel would continue involvement, attributing the statement to Bloomberg. This was within the cutoff window.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The statement confirms continued involvement only at a general level; the snapshot gives no scope, binding obligation, node allocation, customer quantity, or production schedule.

gaps: The original Musk X post and exact post time were not directly retrieved. Newsquawk establishes that the statement was in its feed by 06:38 UTC, but not the original post’s exact time.
The original Bloomberg Tan-interview report was not directly verified. The cutoff-safe source in this record is Benzinga’s pre-cutoff snapshot, which attributes Tan’s statement to Bloomberg.

The reviewed sources do not establish whether TSMC actually subleased space, the precise Intel role, a node-level agreement, a binding production booking, or associated volumes and timing; no direct TSMC statement was found in this focused search.
research_notes: Cutoff used: 2026-10-07T09:04:00.845088Z. The pre-event record in this focused search is an Oct. 2 report that TSMC was exploring a role, followed by Musk describing the contact as discussions only on Oct. 3. On Oct. 7, a time-stamped Newsquawk item relayed Musk’s statement that his companies would build and run the fab, with only a possible TSMC sublease; a pre-cutoff Benzinga snapshot reported Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan saying Intel would continue involvement. These reports clarify public statements but do not establish project terms or binding production commitments. The original Bloomberg Tan-interview report and Musk’s original X post were not directly verified; that limitation is noted below. No post-cutoff reporting or market reaction is used.
